notes.title: Dev Blog 6: Cinema Playtest
notes.notes:
On May 14th, we showcased and playtested [b][i]Dark Queen of Samobor[/i][/b] in Karlovac, Croatia, as part of "Kino, igra, film" (“Cinema, Game, Film”), a national educational initiative organized by the [b]Croatian Audiovisual Centre (HAVC)[/b]. The event was hosted at the beautiful [b]Kino Edison in Karlovac, Croatia[/b].

The goal? To [b]promote locally made games and films[/b] while helping younger generations build media literacy through critical thinking and hands-on experience.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121225/49c2f91ff071729188651c28436df65931718e6c.jpg[/img][i]"Dark Queen of Samobor" at cinema Edison, Karlovac, Croatia
[/i]
We presented [b][i]Dark Queen of Samobor[/i][/b] to two groups of high school students from Karlovac and the response was Incredibly heartwarming. They enjoyed playing the game and they were intrigued by the fact that it draws from Croatian culture, literature, and mythology. Several students told us they were already fans, excited to see [b]August Šenoa and Ivana Brlić-Mažuranić’s stories come to life in this unique, interactive format[/b].

It was amazing to see teens connecting with the game, not just for the gameplay but also for the themes, mood, and cultural roots behind it. This is exactly what we hope to achieve with [i][b]Dark Queen of Samobor[/b][/i], provide a fun and cinematic gameplay experience and spread the word of our own culture and mythology.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121225/2b2016942f584cc0456758adb3f005af71379d4d.jpg[/img][i]Playtessting "Dark Queen of Samobor" with a group of high school students[/i]

[h3]Games Meet Film[/h3]
Alongside our game, students watched and discussed the sci-fi short [b][i]Slice of Life[/i][/b], a [b]Croatian homage to classics like Blade Runner and Terminator[/b]. The screening was led by film educator [b]Silvestar Mileta[/b], who sparked a deep discussion on genre and storytelling. Together, the film and game offered a complete educational experience, showing how powerful and interconnected storytelling across mediums can be.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121225/4ee957f0991da7b4ef8ecb348c313373ae047479.jpg[/img][i]Watching "Slice of Life" on a big screen 1[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121225/ea1165258f4b0ddab5dfd13d0ba715dd21e03f2d.jpg[/img][i]Watching "Slice of Life" on a big screen 2[/i]

[h3]Why It Mattered[/h3]
This was no ordinary playtest. It was part of a [b]national effort to support Croatian creatives and get young people thinking critically about the content they consume[/b]. And maybe even make some of their own one day.

We're incredibly proud that [b][i]Dark Queen of Samobor[/i][/b] is part of this initiative, and we want to thank everyone involved: Kino Edison, HAVC, the schools, and of course every student who sat down to play. [b]You’re our future audience, and your feedback is gold.[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121225/1e8baf9c4df2e8b0edb00a5945e01b4686a15912.jpg[/img][i]Part of Downtown Game Studio team at the playtest - our Sound Designer Matija and Art Director Mato [/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121225/fe2b609db20ea1c4749fc6a2dc811e6deb2dc25e.jpg[/img]Group of high school students playing "Dark Queen of Samobor"

[h3]Back to the Shadows[/h3]
After an inspiring day at the cinema, we’re back into full development mode. Seeing [b][i]Dark Queen of Samobor [/i][/b]in the hands of new players was a powerful reminder of why we’re making this game. But now it’s time to return to the darkness, polish our blades, and sharpen the game further.

We’re already working on something special that we’ll reveal in early June.

Until then, thank you for your support. And keep your lanterns lit.
- The Dark Queen Team

notes.title: Dev Blog 5: Showcasing Dark Queen
notes.notes:
These past few weeks have been a whirlwind but the kind that remind us why we’re doing all this in the first place.

We recently brought Dark Queen to two very different but equally meaningful events: Reboot Develop Blue in Dubrovnik, and Gaming Meetup Osijek powered by BIOS, a local indie initiative we co-organized. Both gave us a chance to put our current prototype into the hands of players, developers, publishers, and other industry pros, and the feedback we received has been inspiring.

[h3]Reboot Develop Blue
[/h3]Reboot Develop Blue is one of the most prestigious games industry conferences in the world. Held in the beautiful coastal city of Dubrovnik, it gathers thousands of professionals from all corners of the global industry, from indie developers to AAA publishers.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121225/acc8bd33cbfec8c8186048ca857ab5b8484121d0.jpg[/img]
[i]Pitching Dark Queen at Reboot Develop Blue
[/i]

We had the chance to showcase Dark Queen to an audience of fellow devs, publishers, producers, and other industry pros. We discovered more ways to improve our gameplay and we got honest reactions to our early build, which were generally very positive. The most exciting part for us was that people kept coming back. Some played more than once. Others brought their friends or colleagues. Even in its early form, Dark Queen is already doing what it’s meant to: pulling players into its dark, strange, beautiful, and threatening world.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121225/00ad47d6b3220ffa8f8b294aa893372ab6b90f44.jpg[/img]
[i]Playtesting at Reboot Develop Blue
[/i]

[h3]Gaming Meetup Osijek
[/h3]Two weeks later, back home in Osijek, we co-hosted Gaming Meetup Osijek, a community-powered gathering celebrating game development in eastern Croatia. We organized it with support from BIOS, our local business incubator, and it featured both an expo section and talks from some of the most respected names in the local industry.

Our art director Mato Vincetić gave a short talk about Dark Queen’s visual direction and worldbuilding, and we were honored to be joined by Davor Hunski, one of the founders of Croteam (yes, Serious Sam and The Talos Principle), who gave a fantastic keynote and reminded us all how far Croatian game development has come.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121225/9b2cab5f46e67047e345265de81d7e70a3f240a6.jpg[/img]
[i]Mato at Gaming Meetup Osijek[/i]


We had our booth set up with the latest build of Dark Queen and got to watch people, from students to experienced developers, explore the game firsthand. Once again, the feedback was encouraging, thoughtful, and very clear: the direction is right, and now it’s time to polish and expand. Big thank you once again to everyone who played our prototype at the event.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121225/7d66fb260be985d016e063c8baf15c61a3552305.jpg[/img]
[i]Playtesting at Gaming Meetup Osijek[/i]


[h3]Thank you for your feedback, it shapes the game
[/h3]We also want to thank everyone who played the game at previous test sessions, like Reboot Infogamer and Blender Film & Games. Around 90% of the changes we made for this latest build were directly based on your input. The game feels tighter, more atmospheric, and just better, and it’s because of what you told us. Everything mattered, from noticing a bug, giving us a mechanic suggestion, or simply telling us what you loved. And it still does.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121225/59b3dd6d6295d62f1af6f13d089fae7f29643601.jpg[/img]
[i]Playtesting at Gaming Meetup Osijek[/i]


[h3]What's Next?
[/h3]We’re deep in development and the next few months are going to be big for us. We can’t share more just yet, but we’re cooking up something special for the beginning of June.

Thank you to everyone who played the game so far, asked questions, and gave feedback. We’re incredibly excited to be building this dark world together with you. 

Until next time,

The Dark Queen Team

notes.title: Dev Blog 4: The Art Behind Dark Queen
notes.notes:
Hello once again, everyone!

In this post we’ll talk about the inspirations for Dark Queen that come from the world of classic cinema and animation. We want to build a world that is both visually enchanting and deeply atmospheric, a world where folklore intertwines with fantasy. Our vision is rooted in iconic animations, and timeless pieces of art that evoke strong atmospheres and unforgettable visuals. We’re blending these influences to shape a game that’s unique in its style, lore, and impact. In this post we’ll take a look into some of the biggest inspirations that are shaping the world of Dark Queen. 

[h2]Visual Inspirations: Crafting a Darkly Enchanted World
[/h2]

From our very first concepts, we wanted Dark Queen to have a mysterious look, mixing folklore with dark fantasy. This is where we turned for visual inspiration:

[h3]80s Dark Fantasy Movies & Animations[/h3]
The 80s were filled with iconic dark fantasy visuals, from the eerie worlds of [i]The Dark Crystal[/i] to the magic atmosphere of [i]Legend[/i]. We were captivated by the way these films handled magic and darkness and how every scene felt alive with unseen threats and hidden beauty. The sense of wonder mixed with menace in these films directly influenced how we’re approaching visual storytelling in Dark Queen.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121225/47f6aff5c9ba904636e846fbc7eb27b120c8f62c.gif[/img] 
[i]The Dark Crystal, Incorporated Television Company (ITC), Jim Henson Productions, Henson Organisation[/i]

[h3]Disney Animated Movies (especially Sleeping Beauty)[/h3]
Disney’s [i]Sleeping Beauty[/i] is one of key inspirations in developing the mythical look of our environments. The grand, stylized approach of its forested settings and gothic architecture inspired the enchanted, haunting aspects of our game’s aesthetic.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121225/e2b00721387d5af4980f5d0dc915319d890b239d.gif[/img]
[i]Sleeping Beatuty; Walt Disney Animation Studios, Walt Disney Productions[/i]

[h3]Conan the Barbarian[/h3]
The world of [i]Conan the Barbarian[/i] and its heroes offers us an anchor in classic dark fantasy. The rawness of the characters, their primal strength, and the intense atmospheric environments inspire much of our character and world design. You’ll also find echoes of this influence in our protagonist, and in general feeling of raw power meeting a world filled with mystery and danger.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121225/d415532697af6613e0e56e177ea74bb20b97efba.gif[/img]
[i]Conan Barbarian; Dino De Laurentiis Company, Pressman Film[/i]

[h3]Čudesna Šuma (The Elm-Chanted Forest)[/h3]
A Croatian animated classic, [i]Čudesna Šuma[/i] is filled with mythical creatures and vibrant landscapes inspired by our own folklore. This film helped us envision a uniquely Croatian take on fantasy, one that feels both familiar and otherworldly. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121225/36a03e8a312aeca54edb33d7d0000401f82e740d.gif[/img]
[i]Čudesna Šuma; Croatia Film, Fantasy Forest[/i]

[h2]Artists Who Shaped Our Vision[/h2]
Besides these film and animation classics, these are specific artists who are making a strong influence in shaping the world of Dark Queen.

[h3]Frank Frazetta[/h3]
Known for his iconic fantasy art, Frazetta’s characters are bold, raw, and larger-than-life, yet grounded in emotion and strength. His work is guiding us in making characters who feel visceral and powerful, embodying the strength and mystique of Dark Queen’s protagonists and enemies alike.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121225/a921faca822682d29717461e20a6c55cf89abe1f.jpg[/img][i]Frank Frazetta, Death Dealer II[/i]

[h3]Eyvind Earle[/h3]
Famed for his work on [i]Sleeping Beauty[/i], Earle’s environmental designs give us a basis for creating captivating and atmospheric backgrounds that feel simultaneously welcoming and foreboding. His influence helps us shape the look of Dark Queen’s world, filled with dramatic contrasts and detailed natural landscapes.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121225/178d37150a2425a5697851f45430cb64478efe0c.jpg[/img][i]Eyvind Earle, Wind Breaks[/i]

[h2]Blending Inspiration with Uniqueness[/h2]
These inspirations are key ingredients in Dark Queen’s world, but we aim to blend them into something uniquely ours. With Croatian mythology and folklore at the core of our narrative, we’re taking inspiration from these iconic sources to shape a new, culturally enriched vision of dark fantasy. Dark Queen is a game that combines classic influences with a fresh setting, a tribute to legends that have haunted imaginations for centuries, while inviting players to step into a world they’ve never quite seen before.

That's all for this post. Stay tuned for more behind-the-scenes insights into the world of Dark Queen as we continue with our development. 

Thank you for following our journey!

Downtown Game Studio team

notes.title: Dev Blog 3: Enhancing the Combat Experience
notes.notes:
Hello again, everyone! 

In today’s post, we’ll talk about our combat feedback system and what we did to “juice it up”.

We wanted to create a combat system that feels responsive, dynamic, and rewarding. It consists of light and heavy attacks with addition of some cool abilities that add depth to the gameplay. In the coming blog posts, we’ll dive into some of these abilities, but today, we want to focus on something just as crucial - the player feedback system that makes combat feel impactful.

Initially, when we implemented our basic attacks, everything worked as expected. You could strike enemies, deal damage, and move on to the next one. But something was missing. The combat felt flat - functional but not exciting. It lacked that “wow” effect that makes each swing of the axe feel powerful and rewarding. We playtested this prototype at Blender: FIlm & Games conference in Zagreb and one of the most frequent feedback was related to exactly that - how the game responded to each hit. With the right combination of visual and audio cues, even the simple attacks can feel more intense and satisfying and here's what we did (so far) to achieve that.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121225/aa7e224f3c453866b788809a0e44eca747d5f66a.gif[/img]
Initial State: No Feedback

[h2]Camera Shake: Adding Weight to Hits
[/h2]
The first feedback mechanic we added was camera shake. The idea here is simple: when you land a blow, the camera shakes subtly, giving the hit more weight. We didn’t want anything too extreme that would make players feel disoriented, but a small, sharp jolt to the camera can create the sensation of real physical impact. Adding camera shake transformed our combat immediately. Light hits feel a bit quicker, while heavy attacks shake the camera more noticeably, reinforcing their power. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121225/a8a381e89a1867f99e6ac267e3be198b676586cc.gif[/img]
Camera Shake

[h2]Animation Freeze: Letting Hits Sink In
[/h2]
Next, we added an animation freeze effect. Essentially, when you or an enemy gets hit, the character animations freeze for a fraction of a second. It’s almost imperceptible, but the impact is significant. That brief pause allows you to register the blow and gives the hit a moment to breathe. It’s like a punchline in a joke, the pause makes all the difference. Player’s attacks feel more deliberate, and you can now experience a microsecond of satisfaction after landing a strike. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121225/e48f8f751f1292ace412cce3b5e51011c88ac497.gif[/img]
Camera Shake + Animation Freeze

[h2]Particles: Visualizing Impact
[/h2]
After that, we added particles to our hit feedback system. When your weapon connects with an enemy, sparks fly, dust kicks up, and blood splatters. This kind of visual feedback further reinforces the power of the strike by giving you something immediate and tangible to see. We played around with different types of particles for different situations: wood splinters when hitting shields, sparks when clashing with metal armor, and more vivid effects like blood sprays when dealing damage to enemies. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121225/bd560f18b4ef5cd8f22fb97c7a429fec527a133f.gif[/img]
Camera Shake + Animation Freeze + Particles

[h2]Blinking and Color Changes: A Clear Signal of Impact
[/h2]
Finally, we added blinking (color changes) for enemies when they’re hit. For a short period after being struck, enemies blink/flash white, signaling that they’ve been damaged. This kind of visual cue is subtle but incredibly effective in providing immediate feedback. It tells you, “Yes, your attack landed.” This effect makes combat feel snappier but also helps you track the flow of battle more clearly. When you're dealing with multiple enemies, seeing them blink on impact provides instant visual feedback that your attack was effective, even in the chaos of larger fights.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121225/2c0b8e71add1b5cafc8b11e4a03c285c4f914d9e.gif[/img]
Camera Shake + Animation Freeze + Particles + Blinking

[h2]Putting it all together
[/h2]
When we combined all these feedback layers - camera shake, frame freeze, particles, and blinking effects - the combat experience in Dark Queen evolved from functional to juicy. What started as basic light and heavy attacks grew into a system where every strike feels impactful, every hit registers clearly, and every fight becomes more dynamic and exciting. It’s not just about dealing damage, it’s about feeling it.

In future blog posts, we’ll dive into the abilities and special moves that further deepen the combat system, but we wanted to start here. Combat feedback is what turns a simple attack into an exhilarating moment, and we’re excited to continue refining it as development progresses.

Thanks for reading, and we hope you're as excited as we are about what’s to come!

Until next time,
Downtown Game Studio team

notes.title: Dev Blog 2: Playtesting & Feedback
notes.notes:
We believe in crafting a game that resonates deeply with our players, both in storytelling and gameplay. This requires listening to you, our community, at every stage of development. Here’s how playtesting has shaped Dark Queen so far and what’s next.

[h2]First Playtest: Blender Film & Games Conference[/h2]
In October, we unveiled the first early prototype of Dark Queen at the Blender: Film & Games conference in Zagreb, Croatia. It was an exciting moment for us as this was the first time players got to step into the dark world we’re building. The feedback we received was invaluable - players praised the game’s atmosphere and story foundation but also provided constructive criticism about areas needing improvement - mostly regarding the combat mechanics. We compiled an extensive list of changes to make the gameplay feel smoother, more intuitive, and engaging. This initial playtest was a reality check, but also a huge motivator - it confirmed we were on the right track while spotlighting areas that needed our focus.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121225/0eb6cf98f884678df5917e5b9b0cebeaaedb1ff2.jpg[/img] [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121225/c6407ea04f2645580a6c929a94a042bedf10e6c8.jpg[/img]
First Playtest: Blender Film & Games Conference

[h2]The Second Round: Reboot InfoGamer[/h2]
Fast forward to November, where we brought an updated prototype to Reboot Infogamer in Zagreb, the biggest gaming event in the region. This version of the prototype reflected many of the changes inspired by October’s feedback and this was a chance to see how a wider and more diverse audience would react to Dark Queen. The response was incredible and we noticed improvements in the overall player experience thanks to the updates and improvements since the previous version. That said, we also uncovered fresh insights. For instance:
[list]
[*]Some players wanted more clarity in tutorial
[*]All of them wanted better balancing (and responsiveness) in combat
[*]And, as expected, a few bugs made themselves known during extended gameplay sessions
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121225/870694ed0623288ed8faab41141707664ade5d0e.jpg[/img][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121225/750d7e544eb7b96609c5f8e1ef59303967769492.jpg[/img]
Second Playtest: Reboot InfoGamer

[h2]Next Steps: Playtesting with Our Discord Community[/h2]
As we reflect on our playtesting journey so far, it’s clear that community involvement has been the cornerstone of Dark Queen’s progress. The next chapter in this process will be even more collaborative: we’ll be opening up playtesting to our Discord community. This will be a chance to involve you all directly in the development process, giving you a sneak peek at the game’s improvements while gathering targeted feedback. We’re especially looking forward to hearing from players who’ve followed our development from these early stages and are deeply invested in seeing Dark Queen move on.

[h2]Your Voice Shapes Dark Queen[/h2]Playtesting is more than just identifying what works and what doesn’t - it’s about building a game with the players, not just for them. Every piece of feedback brings us closer to realizing the full potential of Dark Queen. We want to thank everyone who’s played our prototype so far and shared their thoughts. And to our Discord community: get ready, because you’ll soon have a chance to step into the world of Dark Queen and leave your mark on our journey.

Stay tuned for details on our next playtesting round, and as always, thank you for being a part of this adventure!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121225/f87cd368151ea03c27994c4ec46eb1b1e6fde06d.jpg[/img]

Until the next time,
Downtown Game Studio team

notes.title: Dev Blog 1: Context & Background
notes.notes:
Hello again, everyone!

Today, we're diving into the roots of [i]Dark Queen[/i], a world deeply shaped by Croatian mythology, history, and folklore. In this first post, we'll explore the key inspirations that breathe life into our game's dark and mysterious world.

[h3]The Foundations: Croatian Mythology and Folklore
[/h3]

Dark Queen draws heavily from Croatia's rich tapestry of myth and legend—a wellspring of dark stories and mysteries passed down through generations. Two key elements have particularly influenced the game:
[list]August Šenoa's  [i]Snake Queen[/i] [/list][list]The legends of Queen Barbara of Cilli. [/list]
Let’s take a closer look at each.

[h3]Queen Barbara of Cilli: The “Dark Queen”
[/h3]

At the heart of [i]Dark Queen[/i] lies the legend of Queen Barbara of Cilli, a 15th-century ruler steeped in mystery. Known in Croatia as the “Dark Queen,” Barbara was an empress, alchemist, and powerful figure, feared for her rumored mastery of dark forces. Her reign has inspired countless legends—stories of cruelty, magic, and a deep connection to the supernatural. In [i]Dark Queen[/i], her persona serves as the backbone of the Queen herself, blending history with myth to create a ruler whose power transcends the natural world.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121225/5da9ad7363ccb278cf7aa73e45096a9e82b8185a.jpg[/img]

[h3]The “Snake Queen” by August Šenoa
[/h3]

August Šenoa, one of Croatia's greatest literary figures, wrote [i]The Snake Queen[/i] in the 19th century, a tale that fuses historical reality with folklore, centering on themes of love, betrayal, and tragedy. It tells the story of a noble warrior who loses his beloved to dark forces. This tragic narrative of sorrow and loss resonates deeply with the spirit of Slavic mythology, where human fate is intertwined with both natural and supernatural powers. In [i]Dark Queen[/i], this tale forms the foundation of our world—a place where myth and reality coexist. 

[h3]The Influence of Croatian Mythology and Legends
[/h3]

Beyond the direct influence of Šenoa’s literary work and the legend of Queen Barbara, [i]Dark Queen[/i] is steeped in Croatian and Slavic folklore. These ancient tales introduce a range of Slavic deities, spirits, and creatures, which populate the world of [i]Dark Queen[/i]. As you explore this haunting landscape, you will encounter enemies and locations shaped by these myths—from giants who once battled the gods to vampires lurking in forgotten forests. Each area in the game is infused with the spirit of Croatian folklore, designed to immerse you in a realm where history and myth blur.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121225/2a6a5a24b23eb52b85335ac857fd57d6a53fe474.jpg[/img]

Thank you for joining us on this journey through the depths of Croatian mythology. Where legends live and the line between reality and the supernatural is ever-shifting. 

Until next time,
Downtown Game Studio Team

[/b]

To give something back to you during development, we decided to use this space to talk to you about Dark Queen. To wrap up this introductory post, we want to thank you once again for all of your feedback and comments as every one of them helps us in achieving that goal.

Until the next time,

Downtown Game Studio Team
